B1.title: Sent from the deal's own account
B1.message: The co-signer only signs transactions that move money out of this deal's single-use account, never anything that touches someone else's account.

B2.title: Allowed kinds of transaction
B2.message: Each step may only use the transaction types it needs (payments, closing the account…). Handing control of the account to a new key is never allowed.

B3.title: Network fee is reasonable
B3.message: The XRPL fee must stay under a cap, so a transaction can't quietly drain the account's XRP reserve.

B4.title: Expires quickly if not used
B4.message: A live transaction must expire within a few ledgers (seconds), so a signed one can't be held back and used later. Pre-signed defaults are exempt; they're guarded by the other checks.

B5.title: All-or-nothing
B5.message: When several payments go together, either all of them happen or none do. No half-paid outcome is possible.

B6.title: Pays only people in the deal
B6.message: Money may only go to the guest, the hotel, the arbiters, or the service's fee account, never to an outsider.

B7.title: Closes the account cleanly
B7.message: Closing the account must pay out every last cent and then delete it. If the payouts don't add up to exactly what's in the account, it would leave money stranded.

B8.title: Says which outcome it is
B8.message: Every signed transaction carries a note naming the outcome it executes (agreed settlement, refund, ruling…), so the ledger history explains itself.

B9.title: No other outcome in progress
B9.message: Only one ending can be in flight at a time. If one was just signed and is still settling, a second one waits, so the deal can't be paid out twice.

B10.title: Right token issuer
B10.message: Every amount must be in the real RLUSD token from its official issuer, not a look-alike.

B11.title: The ledger would accept it right now
B11.message: Pre-signed endings can only be tried once: a failed attempt burns them. So the co-signer only signs one when the account is in exactly the state that makes it succeed, including being old enough to be deleted.

C1.title: Confirms the guest's actual booking
C1.message: The hotel's confirmation must point to the guest's own booking request.

C2.title: Right city and dates
C2.message: The confirmed city and check-in/check-out dates must match what the guest asked for.

C4.title: Right price
C4.message: The confirmed total must equal the room price the guest paid in.

C5.title: Deposit within the guest's limit
C5.message: The security deposit the hotel asks for must not exceed the maximum the guest agreed to. Otherwise the confirmation doesn't count.

K1.title: Guest checked in
K1.message: The hotel has recorded the guest's arrival (once recorded, a check-in can't be taken back), and the deposit is in the account.

K2.title: Deposit is exactly right
K2.message: The account holds the room price plus exactly the confirmed deposit, no more, no less.

S2.title: Valid settlement
S2.message: An agreed settlement splits the money between guest and hotel and closes the account, in one transaction.

S4.title: Correct service fee
S4.message: The service takes 0.5% of whatever the hotel receives. Refunds to the guest carry no fee.

S5.title: Guest left a review
S5.message: A stay that happened settles together with the guest's review, so every completed booking leaves a reputation record.

S6.title: Pays only guest, hotel and fee
S6.message: A settlement can only pay the guest, the hotel, and the service fee, never the arbiters or anyone else.

F1.title: Hotel admitted the problem
F1.message: There must be an open check-in dispute from the guest, and the hotel's own statement conceding it.

F2.title: Valid refund
F2.message: A conceded refund sends everything to the guest and closes the account, in one transaction.

F3.title: Full refund
F3.message: Everything in the account goes back to the guest, including any deposit and the dispute bond, with no fee.

R1.title: Refund is due
R1.message: The automatic refund is only for a booking the hotel never confirmed by its deadline. If the hotel confirmed in time, it doesn't apply.

R2.title: The room price is in the account
R2.message: The refund needs at least the room price in the account. Anything more (a stray payment, a deposit) is not a reason to stall: it goes back to the guest too.

R3.title: Valid refund
R3.message: The automatic refund pays the guest back and closes the account.

R4.title: Everything goes back to the guest
R4.message: The guest gets back every last cent in the account, the room price plus anything extra, with no fee.

N1.title: No-show is due
N1.message: A no-show only counts after the last check-in time and after the guest's window to dispute at check-in has closed.

N2.title: Booking was confirmed
N2.message: Only a confirmed booking can end in a no-show. An unconfirmed one ends in a refund instead.

N3.title: Guest never checked in
N3.message: If the hotel recorded the guest as checked in and the deposit is in, it isn't a no-show. A recorded check-in is final: a later 'refused' doesn't undo it.

N4.title: No open dispute
N4.message: If the guest filed a dispute (with its bond), the automatic endings wait for the arbiter. Silence can't override a raised flag.

N5.title: The room price is in the account
N5.message: The no-show needs at least the room price in the account. Anything more (a partial deposit, a stray payment) does not stop it: it goes back to the guest.

N6.title: Valid no-show payout
N6.message: The no-show ending pays the room to the hotel (less the fee), returns anything extra to the guest, and closes the account.

N7.title: Correct service fee
N7.message: The service takes 0.5% of the room price the hotel receives. Money returned to the guest carries no fee.

N8.title: Hotel gets the room, the guest gets any extra
N8.message: The hotel is paid exactly the room price (less the fee). Anything else in the account, such as a partial deposit, goes back to the guest. Of the two no-show endings signed in advance, only the one that fits the money actually in the account can be used.

L1.title: Release is due
L1.message: The 'nobody acted' release only fires after the guest's window to dispute has closed, and only for a stay that happened.

L2.title: No open dispute
L2.message: If the guest filed a dispute (with its bond), the release waits for the arbiter. Silence can't override a raised flag.

L3.title: Room and deposit are in the account
L3.message: The release needs at least the room plus the deposit in the account. Anything more (a stray payment) does not stop it: it goes back to the guest.

L4.title: Valid release
L4.message: The release pays the room to the hotel, returns the deposit and anything extra to the guest, and closes the account.

L5.title: No deposit claim standing
L5.message: If the hotel claimed against the deposit, the release can't just return it: the claim has to be agreed, or ruled on. But the hotel must make its case: if the guest has no open (bonded) dispute and the arbiter hasn't ruled on the claim by the ruling deadline (counted from the end of the guest's dispute window), the claim lapses and the deposit goes back to the guest.

L6.title: Deposit and any extra go back in full
L6.message: The hotel gets the room price less the fee; the whole deposit, plus anything else in the account, returns to the guest.

E1.title: Arbiter missed its deadline on an arrival dispute
E1.message: Only for a confirmed booking the guest hasn't checked into (check-in recorded and deposit paid), with the guest's one open, bonded dispute about a problem on arrival (no room, wrong room), once the arbiter's ruling deadline, counted from the dispute, has passed. An unconfirmed booking is refunded instead; a guest who checked in after all is on the stay or claim track.

E2.title: Arbiter hasn't ruled
E2.message: Once the arbiter's ruling is on record (received by the co-signer), the automatic default never applies: the arbiter and the winning party close the deal instead.

E3.title: Valid refund
E3.message: The entry chargeback pays the guest back and closes the account, in one transaction.

E4.title: Everything goes back to the guest
E4.message: Like a card chargeback, the guest gets back everything in the account: the room price, any deposit and the dispute bond, with no fee.

G1.title: Arbiter missed its deadline on a claim or stay dispute
G1.message: Only for a stay that happened, with the guest's one open, bonded dispute filed after checkout (against the hotel's claim or the stay), in the stay's last night, or on arrival by a guest who then checked in and paid the deposit, once the arbiter's ruling deadline has passed.

G2.title: Arbiter hasn't ruled
G2.message: Once the arbiter's ruling is on record (received by the co-signer), the automatic default never applies: the arbiter and the winning party close the deal instead.

G3.title: Valid payout
G3.message: The claim chargeback pays the hotel, the fee and the guest, and closes the account, in one transaction.

G4.title: Hotel gets the room, nothing more
G4.message: The hotel's claim is rejected: the hotel is paid exactly the room price, less the service's 0.5% fee.

G5.title: Everything else goes back to the guest
G5.message: The guest's payment is the one that sweeps up whatever is left: the whole deposit, the dispute bond and anything extra.

Y1.title: Arbiter missed its deadline on a mid-stay dispute
Y1.message: Only for the guest's one open, bonded dispute filed during the stay, before its last night, once the arbiter's ruling deadline has passed. Stays longer than 14 nights have no such ending: the dispute waits for the arbiter.

Y2.title: Arbiter hasn't ruled
Y2.message: Once the arbiter's ruling is on record (received by the co-signer), the automatic default never applies: the arbiter and the winning party close the deal instead.

Y3.title: Valid payout
Y3.message: The stay chargeback pays the hotel, the fee and the guest, and closes the account, in one transaction.

Y4.title: Hotel gets only the nights used
Y4.message: The hotel is paid for the nights up to and including the one in which the guest disputed (each night's share of the room price), less the service's 0.5% fee. A night counts once it has begun, from the scheduled check-in time. Of the per-night versions signed in advance, only the one for that night can be used.

Y5.title: Everything else goes back to the guest
Y5.message: The guest's payment is the one that sweeps up whatever is left: the remaining nights, the whole deposit, the dispute bond and anything extra.

D1.title: Hotel posted a claim
D1.message: A default ruling only exists to settle a deposit claim the guest never answered.

D2.title: Guest didn't dispute
D2.message: If the guest disputed the claim, the arbiter rules on the dispute instead.

D3.title: Guest's time to answer is over
D3.message: The guest can dispute a claim until the dispute window closes. Only after that does an unanswered claim stand.

D4.title: Claim within the deposit
D4.message: A claim can never exceed the security deposit.

D5.title: Pays exactly the claim
D5.message: The hotel gets the room plus the claim (less the fee); the rest of the deposit goes back to the guest.
